title: Rollout checklist — TP stability (watchdog/quarantine + cancellation/barrier + collective timeouts) — Runtime 1.19.x
body:
Doc purpose
- Single checklist for releasing TP stability fixes into Hosted + Dedicated.
- Covers: preflight, canary gates, metrics, rollback triggers, Dedicated enablement steps, and comms templates.

Scope of changes included (runtime 1.19.x patch line)
- Scheduler: TP-group health model + do not schedule work to quarantined groups (PR 18432)
- Cancellation/barrier deadlock fix for streaming disconnects/timeouts (PR 18441)
- Collectives hardening: periodic async error checks + error propagation (PR 18455)
- Forward-progress watchdog with quarantine + controlled teardown (PR 18462)
- New tuning knobs + defaults by deployment mode (PR 18473)
- Stress/fault-injection harness + CI/perf-canary coverage (PR 18480) + perf-canary workflow (PR 288)
- Observability pack updates (PR 502)

Release owner / decision makers
- Release coord: Connor O'Brien
- Runtime go/no-go: Mateo Alvarez (exec sponsor), Sofia Ivanova (sched), Hiro Tanaka (kernels/collectives)
- SRE go/no-go + guardrails: Rafael Mendes (manager), Sean Gallagher (director)
- Customer comms owner: Henry Cho (PM) + Dev Patel (Support escalation)

Definitions (keep consistent when talking to SRE/Support)
- “Stuck TP group”: watchdog sees no forward progress for threshold while scheduler continues to dispatch OR collective latency exceeds timeout threshold + async error check does not return in time.
- “Quarantine”: scheduler marks TP group unhealthy and stops scheduling new requests; in-flight requests handled per policy (fail-fast vs best-effort completion).
- “Reset”: controlled teardown/recreate of TP group (may coincide with worker restart depending on mode).

Preflight checklist (must be done before canary)
[ ] Version & change list confirmed
- Runtime build: 1.19.(x) with PRs 18432, 18441, 18455, 18462, 18473, 18480 cherry-picked / merged.
- Observability pack deployed: dashboards + alerts in place (PR 502).
- Perf-canary nightly workflow enabled (PR 288) and green in last 24h.

[ ] Feature flags / config defaults reviewed
- Hosted (large pools): watchdog enabled by default; quarantine enabled; conservative thresholds first.
- Dedicated: default OFF unless customer opts in OR we’re doing controlled enablement; keep per-tenant override.
- Private: remain OFF by default until docs + release notes in place; require explicit enablement.

[ ] Runbooks + oncall readiness
- Debugging playbook updated and linked in alert annotations (Confluence: debugging-tp-hangs-playbook).
- INT-611 closed or at least mitigations documented (alerts + paging rules).
- Oncall shift briefed: how to interpret new metrics + expected false positives early.

[ ] Acceptance criteria to ship to canary
- Stress suite passes on staging: no unrecoverable hangs in N runs (see ENG-2405/PR 18480).
- No >2% throughput regression at P50/P95 token latency for representative workloads (ENG-2409).
- New metrics emit consistently in staging/prod shadow for >= 6 hours.

Canary plan (Hosted)
Canary phases
Phase 0: Shadow metrics only (no behavior change)
- Goal: validate instrumentation, alert noise levels, and baseline of “stuck” signals.
- Duration: 6–24h.
- Flags: enable new structured logs + metrics, watchdog/quarantine OFF.

Phase 1: Small canary
- 1–2% of traffic in one high-load region (start us-east), TP-enabled pools only.
- Duration: 12–24h.
- Flags: watchdog ON, quarantine ON, timeouts ON.

Phase 2: Expanded canary
- 10% traffic in 2 regions (us-east + eu-west) with mixed seq length distributions.
- Duration: 24–48h.

Phase 3: Broad rollout
- 50% traffic all regions, then 100% if gates met.

Canary routing notes
- Prefer pools known to hit the issue (high concurrency + long streams).
- Avoid mixing canary + non-canary ranks within a TP group (must be homogeneous at the group boundary).

Gates to move between phases (Hosted)
All must be true for at least 6 continuous hours (unless noted):
1) Customer-visible health
- 5xx rate for TP routes: not worse than baseline by >0.05% absolute (or per SRE threshold per pool).
- Timeout rate (server-side + client cancel correlated): not worse than baseline by >0.1% absolute.
- Streaming disconnects: no increase attributable to server stalls (check correlation with watchdog triggers).

2) Stability signals
- “Stuck TP group” alerts: 0 page-worthy incidents; warning-level alerts acceptable if quarantines auto-recover.
- TP group reset count: within expected envelope (target: <= 1 reset / 1k TP-hours; validate per pool).
- Quarantine events: present (expected) but not thrashing (target: <= 1 quarantine / group / hour).

3) Performance
- P50 decode latency: <= +2% vs baseline.
- P95 decode latency: <= +5% vs baseline.
- Throughput (tokens/sec/GPU): <= -2% vs baseline.

4) Correctness / quality smoke
- No increase in “partial output” / truncated streaming due to cancellations being mis-handled.
- No spikes in “internal error: collective aborted” beyond the expected conversion of silent hangs into explicit failures.

Metrics to watch (dashboards + queries)
Primary dashboards
- “TP Collectives & Scheduler Health” dashboard (Confluence spec: tp-collectives-and-scheduler-health-dashboard)

Core SLO-ish metrics (customer-visible)
- request_success_rate{route,model,deployment}
- request_5xx_rate{route,model}
- request_timeout_rate{route,model}
- stream_disconnect_rate{route,model} (break out client_cancel vs server_disconnect if available)
- p50/p95 latency{route,model} and decode_latency{model}

TP stability metrics (new)
- tp_group_forward_progress_seconds_since_last_step{group_id} (or equivalent gauge)
- tp_group_watchdog_triggers_total{region,pool,reason}
- tp_group_quarantine_total{region,pool,reason}
- tp_group_reset_total{region,pool,reason}
- collective_latency_ms_bucket{op,model,rank,region}
- collective_timeout_total{op,region,pool}
- nccl_async_error_detected_total{region,pool,code}
- scheduler_barrier_wait_ms_bucket{barrier_type,region,pool}
- scheduler_starvation_events_total{region,pool} (if emitted)

Golden correlations (these help triage quickly)
- watchdog_triggers_total vs 5xx_rate (should see hang->explicit failure conversion early; then should drop as hangs eliminated)
- collective_latency p99 vs tp_group_quarantine (comm stalls)
- barrier_wait p99 vs stream_disconnect_rate (cancellation deadlocks)

Alerting expectations during canary
- Expect a small initial uptick in explicit errors as silent hangs become surfaced; this is OK if:
  a) quarantines prevent cascading impact, and
  b) overall customer-visible timeout rate decreases.

Rollback triggers (Hosted)
Immediate rollback (stop canary + revert flags) if ANY of the following:
- Sev1/Sev2 triggered linked to TP stability in canary pools.
- 5xx rate increases by >0.2% absolute for >= 15 minutes in canary vs control (same region/pool class).
- Timeout rate increases by >0.3% absolute for >= 15 minutes.
- Quarantine thrash: >3 quarantines per TP group within 30 minutes OR resets >2 per TP group within 60 minutes.
- Widespread “collective aborted” errors not limited to canary cohort (blast radius leak).
- Latency regression: P95 decode latency +10% sustained for 30 minutes.

Soft rollback / tune-first triggers (investigate + adjust thresholds before rolling back)
- Mild regression: P95 +5% for 30–60 minutes without error rate change.
- Watchdog false positives suspected (quarantine triggers without collective/barrier anomalies).

Rollback procedure (Hosted)
1) Stop further expansion: freeze canary at current %.
2) Flip feature flags to disable quarantine + watchdog (leave metrics/logging ON).
3) Drain canary pools if needed (traffic shift to non-canary pools).
4) If errors persist: roll back runtime build in canary pools.
5) Open incident + link dashboards + attach top logs/traces (see playbook).

Dedicated enablement plan
Principles
- Dedicated customers care about predictable throughput and lower error rates; avoid surprise behavior changes.
- Offer opt-in first with a clear “what changes” + “how to disable” story.

Pre-reqs before enabling for a Dedicated tenant
[ ] Customer environment qualifies (hardware/driver known-good for this patch line).
[ ] Customer is on runtime 1.19.(x) build including PRs above.
[ ] Observability pack installed or at least core metrics exported to their tenant dashboards.
[ ] Support + CSM aligned on comms (ticket updated; rollout window scheduled).

Enablement steps (Dedicated)
1) Identify tenant + cluster(s)
- Record: tenant_id, region, GPU type, driver, model(s), TP degree, peak concurrency.

2) Set flags (start conservative)
- Enable watchdog: true
- Enable quarantine: true
- Collective timeout: conservative default (per ADR-0147)
- Watchdog threshold: start higher (less sensitive) for first 24h to reduce false positives.
- Ensure cancellation/barrier fix enabled (should be code path, not flag; verify).

3) Establish monitoring window
- First 2 hours: runtime eng + SRE in a shared channel, watch dashboards live.
- First 24 hours: check-in at 2h, 6h, 24h; capture counts of quarantines/resets and any customer impact.

4) Success criteria (Dedicated)
- Net reduction in customer-visible timeouts/hangs vs prior week baseline.
- No sustained throughput regression >2% at steady-state.
- Quarantine/resets low and not bursty.

5) Backout plan (Dedicated)
- Disable flags per-tenant immediately (no code rollback needed).
- If needed: roll back runtime build per tenant release process.
- Provide temporary mitigations (see Known Issue page): reduce TP degree / disable long streaming / adjust timeouts.

Comms templates
Template A — Internal: announce Hosted canary start (eng-runtime + eng-sre)
Subject: [Rollout] TP stability fixes canary starting <date> (runtime 1.19.x)
Body:
- Starting canary at <time> in <region/pool>, scope <1–2%> TP traffic.
- Changes: watchdog+quarantine, cancellation/barrier fix, improved collective async error propagation.
- Dashboards: <link name> (TP Collectives & Scheduler Health)
- Rollback triggers: 5xx +0.2% abs/15m, timeouts +0.3% abs/15m, quarantine thrash >3/30m per group.
- Oncall: please note new alerts; see debugging playbook link in alert annotations.
Owner: Connor / Rafael

Template B — Support/CS: customer update for Dedicated opt-in
Subject: Update on multi-GPU TP timeout/hang mitigation (optional enablement)
Body (customer-facing):
- We have a patch release in our inference runtime that specifically targets the multi-GPU tensor-parallel hang/timeouts observed under sustained load.
- What’s changing: improved collective error detection + a forward-progress watchdog that quarantines an unhealthy TP worker group so it stops receiving new work.
- Expected impact: fewer request timeouts/hangs; in some cases, failures may become faster and more explicit rather than silently stalling.
- Rollback/disable: we can disable the watchdog/quarantine behavior per cluster if you see any regression.
- Proposed plan: enable for <cluster> during <window>, monitor jointly for 2 hours, then keep enabled if stable.
Next steps:
- Please confirm your preferred rollout window and whether you want this enabled on all TP endpoints or a subset.

Template C — Incident update (if canary triggers rollback)
Subject: [Action] Rolling back TP stability canary in <region/pool>
Body:
- At <time>, observed <symptom> (metrics: 5xx +X abs, timeouts +Y abs, quarantines thrashing).
- We are rolling back by disabling watchdog/quarantine flags and draining canary pools.
- Next update in 30 minutes with preliminary root cause + whether we need build rollback.
- Links: dashboard, relevant logs, incident doc.

Template D — Release notes snippet (for PM / runtime release note)
- Improved multi-GPU tensor-parallel stability under sustained load.
- Added forward-progress detection for TP worker groups with automatic quarantine/recovery.
- Hardened cancellation handling for streaming disconnects to reduce risk of scheduler/barrier deadlocks.
- Added additional metrics and dashboards to distinguish collective stalls vs kernel stalls vs scheduler starvation.
- New configuration knobs for collective timeouts and watchdog sensitivity (defaults vary by deployment mode).

Owner TODOs (fill before sending to wide audience)
- [ ] Insert actual flag names and defaults once final (PR 18473 merged + confirmed).
- [ ] Add direct links to dashboards in each environment (prod vs staging).
- [ ] Confirm alert thresholds with SRE (Rafael) and update this doc to match.
- [ ] Confirm Dedicated enablement doc snippet with Henry/Dev to align customer wording.

Change log
